title: Road to Perdition
tagline: Every father wants better for his son.
about: A mob enforcer and his son go on the run across Depression-era Illinois.
cue: Serve dessert at the diner stop on the road to Perdition.
faces: Our counter, open all night. It is raining again.
Simmered all day and sliced thick. Buttered cabbage, carrots, boiled potatoes, hot mustard.
Two eggs any style, fried potatoes, toast.
Sharp cheddar on white, fried crisp in butter, cut in fingers. Bread and butter pickles.
Fresh beef mince off the griddle, onions.
Warm buttermilk loaf, salted butter, cheddar.
Drivers must see over the wheel.
We go at first light. M.S.
Deep dish, cinnamon apples, sharp cheddar melted on top.
Hot from the urn, or cold.
Brown sugar, soft cream, Irish style. Strictly medicinal.
Cash only. Pa always pays in cash. No photographers in the dining room.
Prices subject to change. Form 2002. Printed in Illinois, 1931.

Bread and butter pickles.Sandwiches, .15, at the Halfway Diner.How to make it2 Lebanese cucumbers1 small onion150ml white vinegar100ml water60g sugar1 tsp salt1 tsp mustard seeds8 slices of white bread200g sharp cheddar, sliced40g butterThinly slice the cucumbers and onion.Heat the vinegar, water, sugar, salt and mustard seeds until dissolved, then pour over the vegetables.Let the pickles cool and sit while you make the sandwiches.Butter the bread on the outside and fill with the cheddar.Fry over medium heat until golden on both sides. Cut into fingers and serve with the pickles.Irish soda breadWarm buttermilk loaf, salted butter, cheddar.Baked here every morning, .10.How to make it450g plain flour1 tsp bicarbonate of soda1 tsp salt400ml buttermilk100g salted butter200g sharp cheddarMix the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt, add the buttermilk and bring together into a round. Cut a deep cross on top.Bake at 220°C.Reduce the oven to 200°C and bake until golden and hollow when tapped. Serve warm with the butter and cheddar.MainsCorned beef and cabbageSimmered all day and sliced thick. Buttered cabbage, carrots, boiled potatoes, hot mustard.The dinner plate, .31.How to make it1.5kg corned silverside1 onion2 bay leaves6 peppercorns600g potatoes3 carrots1 small cabbage30g butter1 jar hot English mustardPeel the onion, potatoes and carrots and cut the potatoes and carrots into chunks. Quarter the cabbage.Cover the corned silverside with water in a large pot with the onion, bay leaves and peppercorns and bring to a gentle simmer.Simmer the corned silverside gently, topping up the water as needed.Add the potatoes and carrots and keep simmering.Add the cabbage for the last of the cooking.Slice the corned silverside thick and serve with the vegetables, butter and mustard.SweetsApple pieDeep dish, cinnamon apples, sharp cheddar melted on top.Michael, eat your pie.How to make it1kg Granny Smith apples80g caster sugar1 tsp ground cinnamon2 sheets of sweet shortcrust pastry120g sharp cheddar, slicedPeel, core and slice the apples. Cook them gently with the sugar and cinnamon for 5 minutes, then cool.Line a deep pie dish with one pastry sheet, fill with the apples, cover with the second sheet and cut slits in the top.Bake at 190°C until golden.Lay the cheddar on top for the last stretch of baking so it melts.DrinksWake coffeeBrown sugar, soft cream, Irish style. Strictly medicinal.Ask the counterman. Whiskey poured for the dead.How to make it600ml strong brewed coffee160ml Irish whiskey3 tbsp brown sugar150ml thickened creamWhip the cream to soft ribbons so it just holds its shape. Brew the coffee.Warm 4 heatproof glasses with hot water and tip it out.Add brown sugar, whiskey and coffee to each glass and stir until dissolved.Float the cream on top over the back of a spoon. Do not stir.
